title: Siege lock-up fix: re-targeting a soldier to the same spot keeps its queued route
description: Root cause (docs/siege-lockup-root-cause.md): during wall assaults the pathfinder queue holds thousands of per-soldier ground-to-wall-top routes, each unique and uncacheable because it crosses dynamic climbing links. The queue solves about 200-500 a second, so a new request takes 10-20 s to reach the front. But unit re-forms (casualty compaction, squad regroup) re-target every member of a waiting unit every few seconds, and Entity::SetMoveTarget FUN_103DF290 then releases the soldier's still-pending request and appends a new one at the tail. Measured: 400-1,300 requests a second are removed unsolved, against 200-500 solved. Requests are replaced (about every 5 s per soldier) faster than the queue can reach them, so almost nothing completes and every unit near the walls, including the player's, stalls. This hooks SetMoveTarget's first 8 bytes. If the soldier is in movement state 2 (Entity+0x3BC) with a pending, not-ready request (Entity+0x3CC, +0x20 == 0) whose end region (req+0x4C) equals the new destination's region (dest+0x10) and whose end point (req+0x3C/+0x40/+0x44) is within 5 m of the new destination, the call returns (ret 8) and the request keeps its place. Anything else, including NaN distances, runs the original prologue (push esi / mov esi,ecx / call 0x103DD9B0) and continues at 0x103DF298 unchanged. The code is position-independent (relative branches only).
